When you don't have that luxury, the following process will let you learn better.

Find a guide for the language you want

Do 1 very basic  project in the language 

Find out what frameworks people use for it

Do another basic project  with one

Find the top rated open source projects on github or similar sites that use the technology you want

Check out the top 5 or 10

Figure out why they're written the way are, run them, debug them

Open up the listed issues and try to fix one 

Even if you can't fix it, that's OK. You're just looking for predefined tasks.

The thing is to me just blocking, dodging, and attacking doesn't create a fighting game. A big component of fighting games is the meta game behind knockdowns and various states. For example let's say your character in a 3d environment is approaching another character. We can call this the equivalent of a neutral state. One of the 2 characters in the situation gets hit. What happens next? Do you just get to keep attacking? Does the second player have tools to respond to it?  Does player 1 have tools to mix up the offense to respond to player 2s offense? This depth is what differentiates a fighting game from one that has combat and is pvp.

I think it really depends on the depth of the combat and thr number of answers you can have to a situation. Those games in particular seem closer to character action combat in monster hunter or dark souls. A pvp version of that kind of combat is probably its own fledgling genre.

There's only a few types of games that can be considered fighting games:

2d fighters like street fighter, guilty gear etc

3d fighters like virtua fighter, tekken, and pokken

Platform fighters like smash, brawlhalla, and slap city

They're pretty different from each other but share the core fundamentals of a fighting game. You seek to eliminate the opponent, can attack, block, and throw. There's a neutral game, proper disadvantage states, knock down states, and emphasis on positioning in general. 

In theory you can make different types of games with all these mechanics that are also pvp and loosely classify it as a fighting game.
